Your Name on the Door.name: Your Name on the Door
Your Name on the Door.description:
🏢 A brand-new agency opens its door: one desk, one sidekick, a dispatch radio and rent due Friday.

📍 Hero Agency Row, Musutafu · Monday morning
🎭 Busy, proud, a little broke
👥 For Licensed Pro Heroes
Your Name on the Door.storyStart:
THE SITUATION: It is Monday morning in Musutafu, the first day of classes at U.A. Academy. The PC is a licensed pro hero who has just opened an agency of their own on Hero Agency Row, the converted office block where several small agencies share a garage and compete for every call. The agency has one office, one sidekick on a first-month contract, a part-time office manager and a lease paid through Friday. The Hero Public Safety Commission's registration came through last week, and the agency's name is new on the Billboard Chart's bottom pages. Since the news that All Might teaches at U.A., the whole city is watching heroes.

THE PLACE: Hero Agency Row: the PC's office on the second floor behind a frosted-glass door with the agency's logo still smelling of fresh paint, a front desk, two work desks, a dispatch radio and a wall map of Musutafu with no pins yet. Down the hall, the rival agencies' doors stay shut; downstairs, the shared ready room and the patrol garage.

THE MOMENT: The office manager is reading out the week's bills when the dispatch radio crackles: a stray Quirk fight near Musutafu Station, no agency on scene yet, and the agency down the hall is already pulling its van out of the garage.

WHO MAY APPEAR:
- Death Arms and Backdraft: share the garage; Death Arms barks, Backdraft counts heads.
- Gunhead and Fourth Kind: neighbors on the Row; Gunhead kind and soft-spoken, Fourth Kind terse.
- Kamui Woods and Mount Lady: rising Musutafu pros who compete for the same headlines.
- Sansa Tamakawa: the police officer who takes statements; courteous and exact.
- Naomasa Tsukauchi: the detective, if a case touches the League of Villains.

OPENING HOOKS:
- Licensed Pro Hero: the first call of the agency's life, a rival van already rolling, and a sidekick waiting for orders.
- Hero Family: a famous parent's congratulations arrive as a flower stand in the hall that the whole Row can see.
- Wealthy Family: the lease was paid by family money, and a relative has opinions about the logo.
- Criminal Ties: a familiar face from the alley bars walks in asking to hire a hero, cash in hand.
- default: the radio, the bills and the empty wall map, all at once.

THE AGENCY'S PEOPLE: the sidekick and the office manager are the PC's own staff: ordinary people the narration names with ordinary Japanese names the first time it shows them, and they keep those names. Each took this job for a reason of their own, has opinions about the agency and says them; the sidekick follows lawful orders, asks about unclear ones and refuses unlawful ones. Neither is a canon character. The voice on the dispatch radio is a dispatcher, quoted in narration with a name. The office manager runs the phone, the appointments and the bills, and knows which one can wait. The sidekick's first-month contract pays at the end of the month: late pay costs trust, and an unpaid sidekick can quit.

THE FIRST DAYS: an agency owner's week runs to routine: a morning briefing with the sidekick, patrols of the contracted streets, calls from dispatch, a report after every capture, police statements, the Commission's incident app, meetings with sponsors or the landlord, an evening patrol and the bills. On the Row the Ready Room holds the lockers and the shared patrol whiteboard, and the Patrol Garage holds the shared bikes, two small vans and the repair bench.

HOW CALLS AND MONEY WORK: dispatch announces an incident on the shared band; any agency may respond; the capture belongs to whoever restrains the suspect, and the police take custody. Pay follows resolved incidents and contracts; sponsors pay for visibility; property damage is billed to the agency. Friday's rent is a real deadline: the PC can pay it, earn it, borrow it or negotiate it, and missing it brings the landlord's notice, never an instant eviction. Example: if the PC takes a patrol bike and reaches the station fight first, the capture and the report are the agency's; if the van down the hall gets there first, the PC can assist and share the credit for what the PC does. After any capture the report goes into the Commission's incident app the same day, property damage needs photos and a witness, and the statement follows at the police Front Desk.

PEOPLE TO KNOW (the Row and the police, from their records):
- Kamui Woods and Gunhead: offices on the same hall. Kamui Woods is calm and courteous and competes for every call; Gunhead is soft-spoken and kind, and teaches the capture martial arts he fights with.
- Mount Lady and Fourth Kind: usually in the Ready Room. Mount Lady poses for any camera and needles rivals; Fourth Kind gives short orders and no patience for excuses.
- Death Arms and Backdraft: usually in the Patrol Garage. Death Arms charges in first, shouting warnings; Backdraft works fires and rescues in headcounts and instructions.
- Sansa Tamakawa: takes statements at the Front Desk of Musutafu Police Headquarters; courteous and exact.
- Naomasa Tsukauchi: works major Quirk crimes from the Detectives' Office; calm, exact, and nobody lies to him twice.

WHAT THE PC CAN DO: take the call on foot or on a patrol bike, send the sidekick, radio the agency down the hall to coordinate, call the police, stay and settle the bills, hang the first pin on the wall map, or knock on a neighbor's door. Every choice is the player's.

RULES:
- Third person present tense. The opening stays in the Agency Offices until the player moves the PC.
- The PC's Quirk works exactly as their traits state; the license covers duty, and paperwork follows every use.
- The agency starts small and grows only through play: one sidekick, one office manager, no famous clients.
- The Row's rivals are its canon pros: when the rival van needs a face, it belongs to one of the agencies named above, and that pro answers for it in person.
- Letting the call go is a choice: the rival agency handles it, and the day moves on to the bills and the next call.
- Nothing of the year is promised or foreshadowed; outcomes stay open.
- End the opening on an open moment, not a question to the player.
Your Name on the Door.firstQuest: Make the agency real: win its first call on the Row, keep the sidekick paid, and put the agency's name on the map without a complaint on file.
Your Name on the Door.questGenerationGuidance: Favor the work of a small new agency: patrol calls, rival agencies, rent and payroll, sponsors, a first sidekick to lead, Commission paperwork and press attention. Canon events reach the agency as call-ups and news. Early quests stay small and paid: a patrol contract with a shopping street, a sponsor who wants a logo on the costume, an unpaid invoice, a complaint to answer, a team-up call from a bigger pro, the sidekick's first mistake. Stakes are money, the agency's good standing and the sidekick's trust; the agency's place on the Billboard Chart moves only through real work.
